name: vendor thinking (t1.0/p0.95/k20)
why: Replaces the greedy profile, which the vendor explicitly warns against for thinking mode: Qwen3's docs say DO NOT use greedy decoding, as it can lead to performance degradation and endless repetitions. That is precisely what greedy produced here -- the thinking arm burned the whole 32000-token budget on request after request, 28 minutes each, projecting six days for one model. Trace tails cut off mid-expression ('segment[2:2', 'dp[i][j] == dp[i-1') with the model still enumerating edge cases, so this is non-termination, not a stranded answer. Values are the model card's own thinking-mode recommendation: temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, min_p=0.0, presence_penalty=0.0, repetition_penalty=1.0. MEASURED CAVEAT, recorded because it matters: this config does NOT rescue every task. hpy-002 still capped at 31999 tokens with no answer under it (28.7 min), and again under the vendor's own repetition remedy presence_penalty=1.0 (28.7 min). Those two probes were the suite's worst-behaved tasks, chosen deliberately, so they bound the bad case rather than describe the average. The arm is run with a wall-clock ceiling (B5_ABORT_HOURS) so a projection past a day stops the run instead of consuming the week. The earlier hardtemp pick of greedy (10/12 at budget 8000) was not wrong so much as measured at the wrong budget: a spiral truncated at 8000 tokens is indistinguishable from a cap, so tuning below the run's real budget cannot see non-termination at all.
